name: Saint Margaret of Scotland
history: An English princess who married King Malcolm III of Scotland. She reformed the Church in Scotland, founded the abbey at Dunfermline and the Queen's Ferry for pilgrims to Saint Andrews, and fed the poor at her own table before she ate.
meditation: Holiness in marriage and family life: do one thing today for those you live with.
life: Margaret was born around 1045 in Hungary, where her father, an English prince, lived in exile; she was a granddaughter of King Edmund Ironside. The family came to England in 1057, and after the Norman Conquest they fled north. About 1070 she married Malcolm III of Scotland. Of their eight children, three sons became kings of Scots and a daughter became queen of England. Her confessor Turgot, who wrote her life, tells that she rose at night to pray, read the Scriptures, and washed the feet of the poor and fed orphans before taking her own meal. She brought Benedictine monks from Canterbury to Dunfermline and encouraged councils that brought Scottish customs for Lent and Easter into line with the wider Church. Her small Gospel book, once dropped in a river and found undamaged, survives in Oxford. She died in 1093, days after her husband and eldest son were killed in battle.
prayerTo: Saint Margaret, wife, mother and queen, you made your household a place of prayer and your table a place of welcome for the poor. Pray for husbands and wives, for parents and children, and for the peoples of Scotland and England. Help me to serve those I live with, patiently and gladly. Amen.
penance: Before your own meal today, prepare or give food for someone in need, perhaps through a food bank. Read a chapter of the Gospels, as Margaret did daily.
